newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industry sales up 13.12 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industry sales up 13.12 pct in April.

text.p: Brazilian industrial sales rose a record seasonally adjusted 13.12 percent in April compared with March, the private National Industry Confederation (CNI) said.
The 13.12 percent increase was the highest ever monthly rise in industry sales since the CNI began calculating the data in January 1992, the CNI said in a statement.

The CNI said industrial sales were boosted by expectations of greater consumer demand, given that more severe credit restrictions were not imposed. The CNI also cited the greater number of working days in April than in March as a reason for the strong growth in industrial sales.
"For these reasons, economists do not believe that the process of decelaration of industrial growth has been interrupted," the statement said.
In March, seasonally adjusted sales were down 4.45 percent from February.
April industry sales were 13.14 percent higher than in the same month last year, the CNI said. In the first four months of 1997, industrial sales rose 10.12 percent.
The number of people employed in industry fell a seasonally adjusted 0.24 percent from March and was 3.43 percent lower than in April 1996, the CNI said.

The total number of hours worked in industry in April increased 1.21 percent from March, but fell 2.61 percent from April last year, the CNI said. In the first four months of 1997, total number of hours worked dropped 3.92 percent.

The total value of salaries paid rose 2.17 percent from March and was up 2.20 percent in comparison with April 1996, the CNI said. In the first four months of 1997, total value of salaries paid climbed 1.02 percent. ((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
